_readme: Nominal/target values and risk zones for the Portfolio Health gauges. Where a real financial-industry standard exists, it's cited in the note. Where none exists, that's stated too rather than pretending otherwise. Edit freely (ask Claude to adjust during a chat session).

cashPercent.note: No formal external standard for this one - it's a reasoned heuristic, not a citation. This portfolio runs many cash-secured puts, which need cash collateral, so 'cash' here is largely CSP collateral, not idle cash. Zones are wider than a typical buy-and-hold cash-drag guideline for that reason.

topPositionPercent.note: SEC diversification standard for a 'diversified' fund under the Investment Company Act of 1940: for 75% of assets, no more than 5% may be in any one issuer (the '75-5-10' rule). Peg set at that 5% ceiling.

topCategoryPercent.note: The SEC's own definition of 'concentrated' is 25%+ of net assets in one industry/group of industries. Peg set at that 25% line.

totalReturnPercent.note: Peg is the S&P 500's long-run nominal average annual return (~10%/yr since 1926). Important caveat: the value this gauge shows is unrealized total return since cost basis across positions bought at different times, NOT a time-weighted annualized return - so this is a rough directional comparison, not apples-to-apples with a true CAGR.

incomeYieldPercent.note: For context: the S&P 500's own dividend yield is only ~1.1% as of Sep 2026 (long-run average ~1.6-1.8%) - a passive index holder isn't targeting meaningful income at all. This portfolio's dividend + cash-secured-put strategy is deliberately aiming well above that baseline; the peg below is a reasoned target for an income-focused strategy, not an external standard.

assignmentRiskPercent.note: No formal external standard - this is a reasoned risk-comfort heuristic for % of open cash-secured puts currently in-the-money. Lower is more comfortable.
